description: Federal advertising (product code R701) and public-relations (R708) contract obligations in the Media Money Register, optionally filtered by agency (a substring of the agency name or a short form such as DHS or DoD), firm (a substring of a reviewed firm's name as the award records carry it) and fiscal year (2017 to 2026). Returns, for each code, the all-agency series, the largest agencies by fiscal year with every other agency shown as the labelled other-agencies remainder, and the reviewed firms' obligations (FY2017 to FY2026, FY2025 and FY2026, as the register publishes them; every other recipient counted as other); for DHS, its R701 and R708 series, R701 by sub-agency and by reviewed firm for FY2024 to FY2026, and its seven campaign task orders with their dates, obligations and outlays as recorded and their competition fields as printed, with no subaward reported on any of them, so the records do not show which outlets carried the advertising; the Defense Department's share of FY2026 R701; and the register's FEC payee check, counted only. A firm is named only when its UEI is reviewed and its name carries a corporate form. Competition fields are shown exactly as FPDS prints them: the extent competed, the reason for other than full and open competition and the number of offers, or not printed. Each figure is named in its record's own words: contract obligations (a subscription is a purchase order, delivery order or definitive contract), grant obligations by assistance listing, Treasury account obligations, termination actions with FPDS's reason code as printed, and the laws' own text; fiscal year 2026 is as reported through the as-of date, as Defense Department contract records reach USAspending about 90 days late. Every answer carries the register's question note: these records show federal award and account obligations and the agencies' own termination records; they do not show what any outlet published, why an award was made or ended, or whether any payment affected coverage. Every answer also carries the side-by-side caption, the as-of date, each file's date, the source page on morvs.ai and the licence. Where FEC figures appear, the answer quotes the FEC's restriction on the sale or use of individual contributor information (52 U.S.C. 30111(a)(4)). Institutions only: no official, consultant, journalist, treasurer or candidate is named; withheld recipients and the advertising firms whose name is a person's full name appear only as counts. A name that matches only a withheld string answers exactly like a name that matches nothing. No party label is given and no outlet's content is characterised.

agency.description: Optional agency name substring, or a short form such as DHS, DoD or HHS; at most 80 characters; DHS rows show with no agency or with DHS.

firm.description: Optional case-insensitive substring of a reviewed advertising or public-relations firm name as the award records carry it; at most 80 characters.

fiscal_year.description: Optional fiscal year, 2017 to 2026; firm rows are published for FY2017-26, FY2025 and FY2026 only.
